salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the customer needs buttons, touch control, protocol conversion or a cleaner way to trigger room behaviour.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It helps hide technical complexity from everyday users.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Meeting rooms, classrooms, AV racks and controlled presentation spaces.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Talk about the action the user wants, not the protocol.
talkTrack: It turns technical commands into practical room actions.

discoveryPrompts: Who controls the room?

systemIntegrator.label: SI / installer
systemIntegrator.headline: EXP-CON-DAC: deployment and commissioning view
systemIntegrator.pitch: Use this view when the installer needs to confirm what each button, touch action or control command actually triggers in the room.
systemIntegrator.value: Turns the sales conversation into practical install checks: location, cabling, signal direction, dependencies, control and commissioning risk.
talkTrack: Check the practical signal path around Audio, Control before finalising the design.

positioningNotes: Good installer language should make dependencies visible before a quote is issued.
Call out install risk early when the product depends on USB bandwidth, network design, endpoint pairing or control integration.
Use when control simplicity or integration is part of the requirement.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not imply it is plug-and-play where cable distance, USB class, endpoint compatibility, network design or control programming still needs validation.
Do not add control hardware unless there is a clear control task.

consultant.label: Consultant / technical
consultant.headline: EXP-CON-DAC: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the control requirement is real, what user actions matter, and whether this product simplifies or complicates the room.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.
discoveryPrompts: Is this requirement driven by user experience, source/display routing, distance, USB, collaboration, network distribution, processing or control?
What would make this product the wrong choice even if it technically works?
Is the system expected to grow, change rooms, add endpoints, record, stream or integrate with a wider AV platform?
Who controls the room?
What actions should be one-touch?
positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.
Be explicit when the product is technically possible but unlikely to be the most natural choice.
Use when control simplicity or integration is part of the requirement.
avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.
Do not add control hardware unless there is a clear control task.

featureLines: WyreStorm provides solutions for today’s demanding LECTURING spaces.
WyreStorm Essentials converters pack a big punch in features, wrapped in a small package; allowing an integrator the freedom to install in the most discreet of locations.

Because the EXP-CON-DAC falls under the essentials line, you can expect feature rich quality at an affordable price tag. The EXP-CON-DAC is a plug-and-play solution that is comprised of a premium metal chassis, which shows the quality of its construction, matching it's features.
Converts S/PDIF digital audio (PCM) signals from compatible device to analog stereo audio
Supports audio signals up to 24-bit with sampling rates up to 192 kHz
Supported file types: jpg, jpeg, png, txt, pdf, doc, docx

WyreStorm Technologies is committed to protecting and respecting your privacy, and we’ll only use your personal information to administer your account and to provide the products and services you requested from us. From time to time, we would like to contact you about our products and services, as well as other content that may be of interest to you. You can unsubscribe from these communications at any time.
